narrator.name: Targon (SN4)
narrator.role: Subnet team: confidential compute and inference market on Bittensor subnet 4
narrator.one_line: Manifold Labs' compute subnet, one of the first on Bittensor, which speaks in the foundation's marketplace-of-digital-commodities language, criticises the network's Python lock-in and subsidised miners, and frames its own subnet as a confidential cloud in hyperscaler territory.

statements.quote: Bittensor is a powerful platform that seems to be limiting its growth by forcing applications to be locked into one stack.
statements.context: Manifold Labs blog post on rewriting the Bittensor client in Go.

statements.quote: There is currently no standard/language-agnostic format for senders or receivers. This keeps the ecosystem trapped into using Python for almost anyone who wants to build on Bittensor.
statements.context: The same Go post on why Manifold built its own client.

statements.quote: Our aim is to move away from a plateau curve for the subnet, opting instead for an exponential curve where competition is not based on registration.
statements.context: Manifold Team's first monthly blog, explaining the subnet 4 redesign for Targon v2.

statements.quote: Introducing Epistula v2: The first truly open source networking protocol in Bittensor history, designed for secure, efficient, and language-agnostic communication.
statements.context: Manifold Labs release note for Epistula, as listed on its releases index.

statements.quote: Our mission is to make Bittensor that kind of protocol. And to do that, we must think bigger.
statements.context: Manifold 2.0 announcement, after describing protocols that disappear into the background.

statements.quote: We believe we have a small window of opportunity to build the world's first decentralized frontier AI lab.
As of writing, the miners on Targon can afford approximately 1,400 H200s a day. This places us in hyperscaler territory.
There must be substance behind subnets for it to sustain long term
statements.context: Rob Myers, Manifold Labs CEO, quoted by Yogita Khatri in The Block on why investors are drawn to Bittensor.

source.title: The Funding: Why Bittensor (TAO) is drawing in crypto investors

statements.quote: At its core, Bittensor is a marketplace of digital commodities.
statements.context: Manifold Labs post 'No Free Gas' on Targon's compute allocation strategy.

statements.quote: If we opened a gas station and cut our prices to $0, we would expect a line of cars that stretched further than the eye could see.
statements.context: The 'No Free Gas' post explaining why subsidised compute attracts abuse.

statements.quote: There is a problem today in Bittensor, where many compute miners do not actually own their hardware.
statements.context: The 'No Free Gas' post on the shift from individual to institutional mining.

statements.quote: We are working to create a market where every $1 that a miner receives is funded by $1 in organic revenue.
statements.context: The 'No Free Gas' post stating Targon's revenue goal.

statements.quote: Introducing Targon Order Book: A new market mechanism enabling miners to set ask prices for their H200s, creating a more efficient and transparent compute marketplace with predictable hourly rates.
statements.context: Manifold Labs release note for Targon v6.2.1, as listed on its releases index.

statements.quote: At Manifold, we believe the future of AI infrastructure will not be owned by a few centralized labs, but rather powered by a network of independent and economically aligned contributors.
The future of AI will not be gated. It will be incentivized.
statements.context: Closing line of the Manifold Labs Series A announcement.

foundation.mission.summary: Manifold says its mission is to make Bittensor a protocol that disappears into the background, and Targon a market where each miner dollar is funded by organic revenue.

foundation.vision.summary: AI infrastructure not owned by a few labs but powered by aligned contributors; a decentralised frontier AI lab.

foundation.values.summary: Substance behind subnets, and no free gas: subsidies invite abuse.

problem.market.summary: Bittensor's Python lock-in limits growth, and zero-price compute attracts abuse.

problem.institutional.summary: Many compute miners on Bittensor do not own their hardware, which Manifold treats as a structural problem.

opportunity.summary: A small window to build the first decentralised frontier AI lab.

audience.summary: Miners, and specifically mid-sized owners of hardware rather than renters.

positioning.category.summary: Bittensor is a marketplace of digital commodities; Targon is a compute marketplace with an order book.

positioning.reason.summary: The reason to believe is organic revenue matching miner payouts.

positioning.against.summary: Against centralised labs, hyperscalers on scale, and against Bittensor's own single-stack lock-in.

value.functional.summary: Predictable hourly compute rates set by miners.

messaging.h1.summary: The future of AI will not be gated, it will be incentivized.

messaging.proof.summary: Miners affording 1,400 H200s a day; the first open source networking protocol in Bittensor history.

voice.summary: Blunt and engineer-critical of the network's tooling, with homely analogies like the gas station.

relationship.summary: Manifold speaks as an early builder that takes the protocol's growth as its own mission.

language.term.summary: Epistula, TVM, and Order Book are Manifold's own names.

subnet.self.summary: Targon is a compute marketplace in hyperscaler territory that refuses free gas and aims to fund every miner dollar with revenue.

subnet.network.summary: Manifold uses the foundation's marketplace-of-digital-commodities frame for Bittensor, but pairs it with open criticism of the network's tooling and miner economics, and a vision of a decentralised frontier lab.

genealogy.summary: In 2024 Manifold wrote about Bittensor as a powerful platform held back by a single Python stack [sn4-001] [sn4-002], answered with its own Go client and Epistula protocol [sn4-004], and described subnet 4's redesign in terms of incentive curves [sn4-003].

In 2025 the frame widened: Manifold's mission is to make Bittensor a protocol that disappears [sn4-005] and to build the first decentralised frontier AI lab [sn4-006], while Bittensor is a marketplace of digital commodities [sn4-009] where free gas draws abuse [sn4-010] and miners should own their hardware [sn4-011]. The Series A line is that AI will be incentivized, not gated [sn4-015].
genealogy.shift: from tooling critique to market economics and a lab ambition
